maya: Heads up — competitor X shipped per-route model selection for multi-tenant customers. Getting a bunch of inbound asks asking if we can match by EOW. Is this a must-do or can we lean into our differentiators?
owen: saw the thread, thanks. short answer: depends on customer tier. enterprise deals asking for parity; PLG users less so.
raj: +1. Technical surface is not trivial: routing + stateful KV cache + billing attribution. We can hack something with a policy layer but it won't meet latency targets out of the gate.
sophie: for prioritization, what's the ask from sales? any committed enterprise RFPs?
maya: two RFPs citing parity explicitly. Sales says they'll stall without a canary feature.
sales-bot: @maya @owen Captured: ACME corp and Meridian both listed per-route routing as evaluation must. ACME wants POC within 6 weeks.
lars: quick feasibility note: minimal implementation options — (A) simple per-route tag -> model alias and naive routing at API gateway (fast, no cache awareness) (B) runtime-aware routing with KV transfer + warmup (slower engineering but keeps perf).
owen: Option A gets us signals but will increase token cost + latency for some paths. Option B is the long-term proper approach. Estimate: A = 2 sprints (eng small team), B = 6-8 sprints across runtime + infra.
raj: also need to flag rollout risk: A will break assumptions in our batching strategy unless we isolate per-tenant pools. That has capacity/cost implications.
sophie: tradeoffs for PM: ship quick for sales vs protect SLOs and cost model. Can we offer a limited POC that measures customer impact?
maya: propose a compromise: offer A as a gated POC with strict SLA caveats and a runbook that rolls customers into dedicated pools if latency regressions > 15%. Sales ok?
sales-bot: Sales: OK to accept graded POC with clear notes. Need a tight success definition.
owen: success criteria suggestion: 1) 95th percentile latency delta <= 30% vs baseline for POC routes; 2) cost per 1M tokens increase <= 25%; 3) no cache miss ratio > 20% for warmed routes after 24h.
lars: implementation notes: will need a feature flag, routing table, telemetry tag, and billing attribution. Also add a canary limit to 5% of traffic per customer initially.
raj: engineering asks: dedicated spike for KV handoff flows and a small API gateway shim to map route->alias. We can reuse existing rollout infra.
sophie: timeline proposal: Spike (1 week) to validate KV handoff risk, POC build (2 sprints), internal load test, then offer to ACME as beta in week 6.
maya: action items: @owen write RFC for gated POC (due in 48h), @raj scope spike, @lars cost estimate and rollout runbook. I'll sync with sales for ACME expectations.
sales-bot: noted. I'll add ACME to the POC schedule and send legal the updated caveat language.
maya: thanks. keeping this thread to track progress — please post blockers here. :thumbsup:
